summary: This chunk adds a new file, skills/adversarial-review-2/SKILL.md, defining an agent skill for disciplined red-team review of plans, designs, or code. It specifies a six-stage workflow: Intake, Charter (threat model naming harm categories), Attack (three parallel fresh-eyes adversary subagents each assigned a distinct lens), Verify and grade (dedupe, sweep seams, severity-rank findings as Confirmed/Plausible), Report (fixed sections: Verdict, Summary table, Findings, Killed findings, Verification items, Retest list), and Retest (re-run failing scenarios after fixes). It includes gotchas warning against skipping the charter, conflating cleverness with severity, and omitting retest, plus a worked example finding about silent message loss during a broker migration.

claims.text: New file skills/adversarial-review-2/SKILL.md is added with 228 lines.
The skill runs three parallel fresh-eyes adversary subagents, each assigned a distinct lens from the charter's ranked harm categories.
Adversaries never receive conversation history or the artifact's prior review results, only the artifact and charter.
Severity is graded on outcome (Critical/High/Medium/Low), not on how clever the attack is.
Findings are ranked in one strict total order with no ties.
The user decides what to fix; the skill does not apply fixes before the user rules.
This skill is described as the 'systematic sibling' of adversarial-review, differing by having no debate or rebuttals.
claims.anchor: This is the systematic sibling of `adversarial-review`
